security-practices.md 'CRITICAL: Project & User Attribution Headers' rules 1, 2 and 4: the change stops header-injection.plugin.ts injecting X-CodeMie-Client/Repository/Branch/Project on /v1/metrics, leaves MetricsApiClient as the setter of those headers there, and adds a new derivation source for the client type (AgentRegistry ssoConfig.clientType fallback in send-path.ts); the same change edits security-practices.md to add an exception that permits this; no CRITICAL callout or security-review sign-off found in the commit messages in range (PR description not visible to this audit)

findings.title: Attribution change lacks security-review sign-off
findings.problem: On /v1/metrics the proxy no longer injects X-CodeMie-Client/Repository/Branch/Project (including the Cowork 'claude-desktop' override); MetricsApiClient (metrics-api-client.ts:167-175) becomes the sole setter, the client type gains a new derivation source (AgentRegistry ssoConfig.clientType fallback in send-path.ts:36-42), and caller-supplied x-codemie-* values pass through the local proxy unvalidated. security-practices.md rules 1, 2 and 4 make this a CRITICAL change requiring recorded security-review sign-off, and the change edits the guide itself to add the exception; no CRITICAL callout or sign-off appears in the commits.
findings.impact: Attribution headers back per-user/tenant accounting and analytics; the guide makes security sign-off a merge precondition, and a change that rewrites the policy to exempt itself bypasses the review it is meant to pass.
findings.recommendation: Mark the PR CRITICAL, fill in the security-practices.md reviewer checklist, and record security-review sign-off on the PR before merge. The reviewer decides whether (a) the new guide exception making MetricsApiClient the setter of X-CodeMie-Client/Repository/Branch/Project on /v1/metrics is accepted, or the canonical injector should instead read the per-record values through a typed contract, and (b) passing caller-supplied attribution headers through the local proxy unvalidated is an acceptable trust model. This is a human decision; no code edit resolves it on its own.
